head.h1: Dubai Catering Prices Guide: What to Budget for Your Event

opening_paragraph: Catering prices in Dubai are set in two bands. MyCHEF prices the food format on its own from AED 90 per head; a chef cooking and serving on site is AED 700 to AED 950 per head. Add 5% VAT to any total.

Most price guides in this city quote one blended number and leave you guessing which product it describes. This page publishes the list itself: per head, per guest count and per occasion, so you can work out your own figure before you speak to anyone.

replace_in_block.new_heading: The catering price list, per head
new_paragraphs: The format is what sets the price, more than the menu does. Read down this catering price list and find the row that matches how you want the food to arrive.
myCHEF catering food price list, Dubai, per person, pre-VAT Format From (per head) What it covers Staff on site
Working / office lunch buffet AED 90 Hot and cold dishes delivered set up for a team lunch Delivery only
Standard event buffet AED 120 A fuller spread for a birthday, family gathering or office celebration Delivery, setup on request
Premium buffet, BBQ, live stations, canapés AED 150 Grazing tables, a grill, a live counter or passed canapés Chefs and crew on site
Private chef, plated and served AED 700–950 A chef shops, cooks, plates each course and clears down Chef, plus service staff
Tasting menu with wine pairing AED 1,400 Multi-course showcase menu built around your table Chef, plus service staff

The gap between the AED 120 row and the AED 700 row is labour, not food quality. A drop-off buffet buys you ingredients, cooking and a van. A plated dinner buys you a chef standing in your kitchen for five hours and a team that plates, serves and washes up. Decide which of those you are buying first, then choose the menu, because the format sets the floor for everything above it. Add 5% VAT to any total.

Two numbers belong with that list, and most caterers here make you ask for them. The volume formats — delivery, working lunch, drop-off — start at 10 guests ; a full buffet starts at 20 ; and any order has to reach AED 900 before VAT. The private chef row is the exception: it is priced per head, so there is no minimum headcount on it at all.

new_paragraphs: Send the same brief to every guest you are considering: date, guest count, venue, service format, rough menu direction and any dietary requirements. Ask for the quote itemised into food, staffing, rentals, delivery and VAT. Ask what happens if the guest count moves by ten either way, and when final numbers are due. Those answers are as informative as the price.

Then look past the number at who is cooking. No chef reaches event catering prices without clearing identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing reviews from earlier clients. catering prices guide , or see event catering to start a brief.

add_block.new_heading: Catering prices in Dubai for a birthday party, a wedding or a small party
new_paragraphs: A birthday is priced like any other event, because the occasion changes the mood and not the arithmetic. A birthday buffet for thirty starts at AED 120 per head, or AED 150 once you add a live station or a grill, and the fixed Birthday Celebration package covers eight to twelve guests from AED 3,600. See birthday catering for the menus.

Wedding catering prices in Dubai are set on the same two bands. A premium buffet or canapé reception starts at AED 150 per head; a plated dinner cooked and served on site is AED 700 to AED 950 per head. We publish no separate wedding rate card, because guest count, venue access and service style move the number far more than the occasion does. Work through the wedding catering checklist before you ask anyone for a figure.

Small party catering in Dubai is where hosts get caught out. Our drop-off and delivery formats start at ten guests, a full buffet at twenty, and any order has to reach AED 900, because trays, transport and setup cost the same for six guests as for sixteen. For a table of two to eight there is no minimum to clear: a private chef is priced per head and gives you more food per dirham than a buffet you cannot fill. add_block.new_heading: How much is the average cost of catering in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Asking for the average cost of catering is like asking for the average price of a car. Our own entry points are AED 90, AED 120 and AED 150 per head by format.

For the wider market, we read 58 per-head prices published on five Dubai caterers' own menus in July 2026. The middle sat near 130 dirhams a head, the quarter mark near 98, and the full spread ran from about 40 for a coffee break to 570 for a six-course plated dinner. Our AED 90 working-lunch tier sits inside the corporate-lunch band those menus occupy. Our chef-led service sits above the plated benchmark, which is what a named chef cooking in your own kitchen costs.

A note on what those figures mean: a per-head price is a starting rate for a defined menu, not a promise about your event. Change the protein, the number of stations or the service hours and the rate moves. Compare quotes on one identical brief and the differences stop being mysterious.

add_block.new_heading: Cheap catering in Dubai, affordable catering, and the difference
new_paragraphs: Cheap catering in Dubai exists, and some of it is fine. What you give up is usually staffing, portion size or the licence trail behind the kitchen. Affordable catering is a different target: the same food, delivered in a format that carries less labour. Four moves cut the per-head figure without thinning the plate.
Change the format, not the menu. Moving a plated dinner to a buffet takes out the service brigade, which is where the money sits.
Grow the guest list. Fixed costs spread. Twenty covers is cheaper per head than eight.
Move the date. November to March is peak season across Dubai; a weekday slot outside it prices better.
Cut a course, not the quantity. Dropping a dessert station costs a guest nothing they will notice. Under-ordering does.

The best way to judge an affordable catering quote is per head after VAT, on the same guest count, with staffing listed as its own line. A headline number that hides the crew is not a lower price, only a later invoice.

add_block.new_heading: Why VAT and licensing sit behind every honest quote
new_paragraphs: Two things stand behind a legitimate figure. VAT comes first: catering and restaurant services in the UAE are taxed at the standard 5% rate, introduced across the country on 1 January 2018, according to the UAE Ministry of Finance . A transparent proposal shows the pre-tax figure and the 5% separately, and every number on this page is pre-VAT.

Compliance is second. Licensed caterers meet the Dubai Municipality Food Code, and the Municipality monitors food establishments, investigates food-borne illness and licenses new food businesses. A quote well under the bands above may be skipping the standards that keep your guests safe.

add_block.new_heading: The three levers behind every quote
new_paragraphs: Once you see the levers, quotes stop looking arbitrary. The first is the menu: course count and ingredient tier. Wagyu, fresh seafood and a live sushi counter push a number up quickly, while a well-built mezze or grill menu delivers generosity at a lower cost. The second, and the largest, is the service level. A drop-off tray needs almost no labour; a plated dinner needs a kitchen brigade, waiters and runners. Labour, not food, is the biggest line on most event quotes.

The third is guest count, and it usually works in your favour. Fixed costs — transport, setup, the chef's time — spread across more covers, so the price per head falls as the event grows. That is why a dinner for eight can cost more per person than a reception for eighty. If your count is uncertain, ask for the price at two or three headcounts so you can see the curve instead of a single figure.

add_block.new_heading: Dubai event catering prices by format in 2026
new_paragraphs: Drop-off catering is the entry point: food delivered ready to serve, no staff, no setup. Buffet service adds presentation and a small team to maintain it. Grazing tables and canapes sit slightly above, since styling and prep hours rise. Live cooking stations add a chef per station and take you into the middle band. Plated multi-course service is the highest per head, because you are also paying for the people who plate and serve every course.

Across those formats most Dubai event catering begins from around AED 700 per person. Private-chef dinners at home run about AED 700 to 950 per person for most menus. Tasting menus and fine-dining formats begin from about AED 1,400 per person. For larger events the per-head figure gives way to a total, with minimums of AED 2,400 or AED 3,600 common, and AED 4,500 and above for large plated galas once rentals and styling are included. Our packages and chef prices show the grouped options.

add_block.new_heading: What is not in the headline number
new_paragraphs: This is where quotes diverge, and it is worth checking line by line. Staffing is sometimes quoted separately from food, which makes a headline price look lower than the comparable one next to it. Rentals — crockery, glassware, linen, furniture — are frequently excluded for venues that have none. Delivery and setup can be a separate line for out-of-area venues, and a temporary kitchen at a venue without one is typically an extra.

Then there are the quiet ones: vendor meals for photographers and musicians, children's portions, corkage or bar coordination, waste removal where the venue requires everything to leave, and overtime if the event runs past the contracted hours. None of these are unreasonable, but they should be visible. A useful test when comparing two quotes: ask both caterers to price the same brief with the same inclusions, then compare the totals instead of the per-head figures.

add_block.new_heading: How VAT and licensing sit inside the price
new_paragraphs: VAT is clear and non-negotiable. Catering and restaurant services in the UAE carry the standard 5% rate, introduced on 1 January 2018 according to the UAE Ministry of Finance . A transparent proposal shows the pre-tax figure and the 5% as separate lines. If a quote does not mention VAT at all, ask before assuming it is included.

Licensing sits behind the price in a less visible way. Licensed caterers work to the Dubai Municipality Food Code, which covers food transportation and delivery vehicles as well as kitchen handling, and requires establishments to run a structured staff training system. The Dubai Municipality Food Safety Department monitors food establishments and investigates food-borne illness, so compliance is checked in practice. Compliance costs money — cold-chain transport, trained staff, proper holding equipment — and a quote materially below the others is often cheaper because one of those is missing.

new_paragraphs: Dubai's event calendar is seasonal, and that affects both availability and what you can do. The outdoor season runs November to March, when days average around 27°C and nights fall to about 19°C ( Weather and Climate ). Those months carry weddings, galas and the conference run at the same time, so the popular dates commit early. The Dubai World Trade Centre , which describes itself as Dubai's epicentre for events, opens a new Dubai Exhibition Centre in 2026, adding further pressure to the same weeks.

Practical timing tips: book peak-season dates as far ahead as you can, and consider a weekday for a corporate event, since weekends carry the private-event demand. Ramadan and the festive period have their own patterns and their own menus. Off-peak summer events held indoors are the most economical time to host, because both venues and caterers have availability.

new_paragraphs: How much is dinner for 2 in Dubai?

With a chef cooking at your table, a dinner for two prices at AED 950 to AED 1,300 per person, because one chef's evening is shared between two covers instead of ten. The set Date Night package is the cheaper route at that size: from AED 1,200 for both of you, covering a three-course menu, the chef, table service and the cleanup. Add 5% VAT.
Is 500 AED enough for food in Dubai?

As a total catering budget, 500 dirhams feeds about five people at our working-lunch buffet rate of AED 90 per head, before VAT. As a per-head budget it clears every buffet tier we publish, including the premium buffet, BBQ and canapé tier at AED 150. It does not reach a chef cooking and serving on site, which starts at AED 700 per person.
How much is the average cost of catering?

There is no single average, because a drop-off buffet and a plated dinner are different products. Our own entry points are AED 90 per head for a working lunch, AED 120 for a standard event buffet and AED 150 for premium buffet, BBQ or canapés. Across 58 per-head prices published by five Dubai caterers in July 2026, the middle of the market sat near 130 dirhams a head, with the range running from about 40 to 570.
How much do catering cost for a party in Dubai?

Multiply the per-head rate by your guest count, then add 5% VAT. Twenty guests on the standard event buffet at AED 120 per head is AED 2,400 before VAT. The same twenty guests with a chef cooking and plating on site starts from AED 600 per person once you pass twenty covers.
What are catering prices in Dubai for a birthday party?

Two routes. Per head, a birthday buffet starts at AED 120, or AED 150 if you want live stations, a BBQ or passed canapés. As a fixed package, the Birthday Celebration covers 8 to 12 guests from AED 3,600 and includes canapés or a starter, a main course, dessert and service staff.
What do wedding catering prices in Dubai look like?

A wedding is priced on the same per-head bands as any other event, so the format decides the figure: from AED 150 per head for a premium buffet, BBQ or canapé reception, and AED 700 to AED 950 per head for a plated dinner cooked and served on site. We publish no separate wedding rate card, because the guest count and the venue move the number more than the word wedding does.
How much do you get paid catering in Dubai?

That is a jobs question rather than a pricing one, and myCHEF does not publish chef or crew pay rates. What it tells you as a host is where your money goes: staffing is the single biggest gap between a AED 120 drop-off buffet and a AED 700 plated service. Chefs who want to work with us can apply through the become a myCHEF page.
What is the minimum headcount for catering in Dubai?

Ours is published, which is more than most caterers here will tell you before a phone call. Delivery, working lunch and drop-off start at 10 guests; a full buffet starts at 20; and any order has to reach AED 900 before VAT. The private chef has no minimum headcount at all, because it is priced per head: two guests run AED 950 to AED 1,300 each, six run AED 750 to AED 1,000.
Is VAT included in catering prices in Dubai?

No. Every per-head figure on this page is pre-VAT. Catering and restaurant services in the UAE carry 5% VAT, introduced on 1 January 2018, and an honest proposal shows the pre-VAT figure and the 5% on separate lines.
What is the cheapest catering format in Dubai?

Drop-off and the working office lunch buffet, from AED 90 per head. They carry no service staff, so you pay for food, packing and delivery rather than for a brigade on site. Below that price point you are usually buying smaller portions rather than a better deal.
How do I get an exact quote?

Send your date, guest count, venue and rough menu direction. You get an itemised proposal back, usually within one business day, with food, staffing, equipment and VAT on separate lines so you can compare it line by line against anyone else's.
